cohort: 730 term neonates with indirect hyperbilirubinemia at the Neonatal ICU of National Institute of Child Health, Karachi, of which 63 underwent exchange transfusion
finding: The most common causes of hyperbilirubinemia requiring exchange transfusion were sepsis (30.2%) and ABO incompatibility (20.6%), with common adverse events including hypokalemia (15.9%), thrombocytopenia (15.9%), and sepsis (9.5%), and a mortality rate of 7.9%.
